sales.title:
AKSUMITE KINGDOM. Endybis, ca. A.D. 270-300. AV Chrysos (Unit) (2.69 gms). NGC Ch EF, Strike: 5/5 Surface: 4/5.
Munro-Hay-1; Anzani-1. Obverse: Draped bust right, wearing skullcap, framed by grain ears; pellet in crescent above; Reverse: Draped bust right, wearing skullcap, framed by grain ears; pellet in crescent above. A beautifully struck example of the type. Highly original surfaces bearing a hint of tone and some light earthen deposits which lend it a charming rustic appeal.

Struck to a weight roughly equivalent to half of the contemporary Roman Aureus, these gold issues of king Endybis are among the very first coins ever produced in Sub-Saharan Africa. The more prolific coins of later Aksumite kings featured Christian imagery and were struck to a reduced weight standard to mirror Roman monetary reforms, making this early emission a rather singular and historic type.
Ex: Freeman & Sear 14 (6/2007), Lot # 295.
